directions.description: Restrict the vector-field class to those with a flow-invariant skew-product/triangular fibered structure, so cross-coordinate nilpotent terms have a canonical, order-respecting home instead of requiring an ad hoc gluing map.
directions.routes_around: Melchior gap (cross terms have no home) and Balthasar vacuous-or-trivial (symmetric coupling forces undefined-or-collapse); avoids inventing a third patched gluing reading of R1/R2.
directions.heuristic: One-directional coupling is a genuine third class distinct from Balthasar's diagonal (no content) and symmetric-coupled (undefined/collapses) cases.

directions.description: Pivot from per-coordinate splitting to Round-0 item (j): test naturality/invariance of jet transport under replacing a Weil algebra by a non-canonically-isomorphic same-dimension one.
directions.routes_around: Balthasar's §5c non-canonicity finding (exterior algebra vs all-cross-terms-zero algebra give inequivalent dynamics); reframes the exact defect found as the subject of the claim.
directions.heuristic: [HEURISTIC] Turns a side-defect discovered in Round 1 into the primary object of study, avoiding the coordinate-splitting typing problem entirely.

directions.description: Import the literature's two-Weil-algebra fibered bundle functor (Kolar-Michor-Slovak style T^{A,B} for a fibered manifold p:Y->M, base algebra A + fiber algebra B with built-in compatibility) as the formalization of 'fibered extension', replacing the ad hoc n-independent-algebras construction.
directions.routes_around: Melchior's untouched literature-comparison subtask; replaces the no-compatibility-structure construction that produced the typing failure with one that has compatibility built in by definition.
directions.heuristic: [HEURISTIC] A published base/fiber construction needs only one compatibility datum, not pairwise compatibility among all n per-coordinate algebras; unconfirmed whether jet-transport-style properties have been checked against it.

directions.description: Abandon per-coordinate splitting for the sibling Round-0 axis (f), initial-value extension, using a single Weil algebra along the initial-value direction with no per-coordinate splitting at all.
directions.routes_around: Casper's likely-misframed finding that (g) was chosen from an uncommitted menu without argued priority over (f)/(h); sidesteps the multi-algebra compatibility problem by construction (only one algebra used).
directions.heuristic: [HEURISTIC] Round 0 already flagged (f) as the most classically grounded entry point with closer literature precedent (variational-equation/flow-Jacobian prolongation), so it was never exposed to Round 1's obstruction.
